Carla: quick heads-up — ran an early-hint handshake pass on llama3-13b-8bit to see if we can shave tail latency without touching kv-cache policy. used the 'earlyhint' handshake filter (lightweight prefix probe) on redwood-qc-1k.
Ben: nice, quick numbers?
Carla: gist — p50 token latency dropped from 62ms -> 44ms, p95 from 210ms -> 150ms. throughput for short prompts up ~18%.
Maya: that's promising. what about quality? any regressions on our QA prompts?
Carla: small hit on exact-match for code-snippets: 0.9% absolute drop on qc-code-200. nlg BLEU-ish proxies down ~0.4. general perplexity on holdout unchanged.
Jin: did you run with quantized kernels only or mixed fallback?
Carla: mixed. runtime opts for int8 kernels when handshake confidence >= 0.8, otherwise fp16 decode. config: 
```
# quick-run command
python rrunner/eval_harness.py \
  --model llama3-13b-8bit \
  --evalset redwood-qc-1k \
  --handshake earlyhint --handshake-thresh 0.8 \
  --batch 1 --max_tokens 256 --kv_policy auto
```
Carla: and added a canary that falls back to fp16 model if the handshake flips in-flight.
Ben: can you paste the mini-diff of the handshake code? curious about where latency gain comes from.
Carla: short version — we prime a 4-token lookahead on a cheap head to predict continuation entropy. if low entropy, we proceed to decode on quant-kernel with prefilled prefix; if high, skip handshake and send normal fp16 path. code is tiny: 
```
def early_hint(prefix):
  h = cheap_model.score(prefix[-4:])
  return h.confidence > thresh
```
Maya: so mostly catching easy continuations early. explains latency wins on short Q/A.
Jin: any stability issues? crashes, kv-mismatch, staleness?
Carla: saw one kv-staleness spike in long-dialog sessions (N=3/500): reuse of cached kv from quant run produced slight token mismatch at decode boundary. fixed by tagging kv with handshake-run-id and invalidating on fallback.
Maya: good. did you test with streaming client? early-hint could change chunk boundaries.
Carla: yes. streaming still fine after adjusting flush to wait for first quant token to commit. slight 6-8ms extra jitter on first byte but overall p50 still lower.
Ben: what about cost impact? GPUs?
Carla: unit tokens per-second on ded pool increased ~12% so cost/token down roughly 9% in our baseline traffic mix.
Jin: ops-bot, can we run a small canary rollout on dedicated pool 3 (eu-west)?
ops-bot: canary request accepted — scheduled 1h window on dedicated-pool-3, 10% traffic. use rollout id rh-earlyhint-1766.
Maya: sweet. next steps: 1) run full qc-extended (10k) with handshake on 2) run targeted safety checks (hallucination blasts) 3) shadow long-dialog for kv-stability for 24h.
Ben: also add a holdout where handshake is forced=always to measure worst-case quality delta.
Carla: agreed. I'll post results in this thread once 10k run finishes. attaching quick CSV snapshot (p50,p95,exact_code,bleu,ppx): 44,150,86.1,28.4,12.3 vs baseline 62,210,87.0,28.8,12.2
Maya: thanks — small tradeoffs. if safety checks pass, green to canary. :thumbsup:
Carla: one more note — this is intentionally conservative handshake logic; we can try hybrid where handshake threshold is workload-specific. leaves room for more unit-econ wins.
Ben: nice work. when you post the 10k results, include a breakdown by prompt length bucket (<32,32-128,>128). that'll help ops sizing.
Carla: will do.
ops-bot: reminder: canary rollout will emit metrics to /dash/earlyhint-rh-1766 every 15s.
Jin: ping me if kv-tagging instrumentation needs a patch release.
Carla: thanks all. followups in ~2h (10k run ETA).
